pages.title: The genome
pages.text: Each farm animal has four genes from 0 to 10: productivity, size, resistance and fertility. Offspring inherit the average of their parents, sometimes with a mutation of plus or minus 1. The livestock ledger shows the genes on right-click.

pages.title: Daily needs
pages.text: Satiety and health drop each cycle (20 per MC day). At zero satiety, health loses 1 per cycle: 5 MC days before death from full health. A grazing animal feeds on grass outside winter. A full trough feeds nearby animals.

pages.title: Feed
pages.text: Feed mix: barley, corn and soybean give 3 units. Silage: a hay bale and corn give 4 units. A well-stocked trough prevents underfeeding.

pages.title: Breeding and the nesting box
pages.text: Breed in spring and summer, with a satiety of at least 40. The nesting box (8 slots, made of planks and wheat) receives eggs from hens and ducks. Place it near your animals.

pages.title: Health
pages.text: Overcrowding and underfeeding cause illness; prolonged dampness brings parasites. The veterinary kit treats an animal. A salt lick nearby restores 1 health point each cycle.

pages.title: The duck
pages.text: The duck, male or female, swims and lays eggs. Its eggs, raw or cooked meat, and other products depend on its genome and feeding.
